headline: Three days off the trail with no run logged yet. Absorption is genuine, not delayed — steps stay high, but structured work is fully paused. The first easy run remains the real test.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is one of a deep block still being digested. Running has gone quiet since the multi-day trail crossing, and that silence is the correct response to the load absorbed over those back-to-back ultra days — not a gap to worry about. Strength has not re-entered the log, which now stretches the layoff long enough that it's worth naming: the concentrated foot volume has eased, but the barbell hasn't returned to fill the space. Steps stay strikingly high even on rest days, so this is not true inactivity — the athlete is simply moving all day without formal sessions, which is a legitimate form of active recovery here. The load metric reads flat because nothing structured has been logged, and that's expected given where you are in the cycle. This is a genuine trough by design, not a decline.
sections.trends: The medium-term shape is a large, deliberate build peaking in the recent trail block, and the sheer year-over-year distance gap shows how much base has been laid down compared to the same point last year. The recent four weeks dwarf the prior four — that's the trail block's fingerprint, not a sustainable steady state. What you'd expect to see next is a controlled step down as the body reabsorbs, then a return to the interleaved rhythm. That shape fits the standing goal of durable year-round capacity: a big concentrated stimulus followed by absorption is exactly how you consolidate a gain rather than fray it.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its anchoring heart rate are unchanged from the baseline, which is neither surprising nor concerning — the recent block was entirely about controlled-HR durability, with essentially no work anywhere near threshold. Nothing in the last stretch was designed to move that number, so its stability is simply confirmation that the speed end has been parked, not lost. When the interleaved rhythm returns and faster work re-enters, that's when this figure becomes informative again. For now it's a stable reference point, not a live signal.
sections.zones: Every recent run sat almost entirely in Z1, with only trace minutes drifting into Z2 — the textbook signature of a long-duration, time-on-feet block executed with discipline. There's no grey-zone creep here at all, which is exactly what you want when the goal is accumulating controlled hours rather than sharpening. The single day with the highest average pushed slightly higher but still held its shape. The intensity distribution matched the block's intent cleanly throughout; nothing ran hot when it should have stayed easy.
sections.hr_comparison: The most recent strength sessions show the usual pattern for this kind of functional work — moderate averages with brief excursions upward, consistent with circuit-style efforts rather than heavy low-rep lifting. Nothing in the strength HR data stands out as unusual against your own history. There's no meaningful sensor-source disagreement worth flagging today.
sections.calendar: The calendar has clearly shifted out of its continuous-running phase — the dense run block has given way to consecutive days without formal training. This is the interruption to the interleaved rhythm I flagged earlier, and it's still ongoing rather than resolved. The question that carries forward is whether the return brings strength and running back in alternation, or whether one modality resumes while the other stays dormant. The high daily movement means the calendar's blank days aren't sedentary — they're just unstructured.
sections.personal_bests: None of the current bests are within reach in this phase — they all live at the speed end, and the recent training has been the opposite quality. The short-distance PBs from last late-summer remain the standing targets, and they'll only become relevant again once fast work re-enters and threshold gets stressed. For now the training focus and the PB list are pointed in different directions, which is fine and expected mid-absorption.

watch_items: Watch whether the first logged run comes back at a normal easy-pace HR, confirming the block absorbed cleanly rather than lingering as fatigue.
Watch whether strength finally re-enters the log — the layoff is now long enough that its continued absence would be a pattern, not just a gap.
Watch whether the return to training reinstates the interleaved run/strength rhythm rather than restarting continuous running volume.
Watch whether the high all-day step count settles as formal training resumes, or whether it stays elevated as a persistent background load.
